title: Sweden's Government Offices block ChatGPT and Claude on staff computers
subtitle: Starting today, officials inside the Prime Minister's Office and the ministries can no longer reach OpenAI's and Anthropic's chatbots directly — only Microsoft Copilot survived the information-security review.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Sweden's Government Offices — the central administration that houses the Prime Minister's Office and every ministry — began blocking the public ChatGPT and Claude services on staff work computers today, Monday October 26, 2026. Microsoft Copilot stays, as the only AI tool approved for all employees after a security review and tightened settings. Mikael Wettercrantz, digitalisation director for the Government Offices, cited the risks of using AI services 'without a formal contract' and pointed to several unspecified incidents of problematic use. A smaller group of staff retains access to the underlying ChatGPT and Claude models through the Intric platform, which is contracted and governed.

The decision was first reported by Sveriges Radio's Ekot news program on October 23 and confirmed to SVT by email. It is narrower than a full chatbot ban: the block appears to target the public browser-based services rather than every API that runs on top of the same models. The practical effect is that Swedish civil servants who had been pasting ministerial text into chatgpt.com or claude.ai will have to stop. The Tax Agency and the National Board of Institutional Care have already imposed similar restrictions, the Enforcement Authority is preparing one, and the European Parliament disabled the same three products on its devices back in February.

The pattern across European governments is converging on the same answer. If the AI service is not under a signed data-processing agreement with specified residency, retention, and audit terms, it does not get to touch government work. Copilot survives because Microsoft already carries the enterprise contract rails that governments have spent two decades hardening around Office 365. Anthropic's Claude models are available inside Copilot through its 2026 integration, but Sweden has not disclosed whether that specific route is enabled in its own deployment. Open-model Chinese entrants face the same procurement wall from the other direction.

A note for learners: 'is this chatbot allowed at work' is becoming a procurement question, not a product one. The capability of ChatGPT and Claude is not what Sweden is objecting to — the contract wrapper is. If you work in or sell to the public sector, the differentiator is no longer which model scores highest on a benchmark; it is which provider has the enterprise agreement, the regional data residency, and the audit log your buyer's information-security office requires. Learning to read a DPA is now closer to the frontier skill than learning to prompt.
